tips.comment: So Sassy is making her handicap debut in the 1:47 at Lingfield, and the booking of Oisin Murphy catches the eye. This three-year-old filly showed promise in her three starts last autumn, notably finishing fourth at Kempton over 6 furlongs, just 2 lengths behind the winner. If she builds on her earlier efforts, she could be a strong contender today.

19 days ago saw the Marco Botti-trained 3yo return from a 181-day break on handicap debut. Ridden by Hollie Doyle (again today), she had obviously trained on, finishing 4th of 12, beaten just over a length. She was strong at the finish and should be more of a finished article today and can break her maiden tag.
I'm hoping George Bass's 3lb claim will get Alcazan in the mix here at Lingfield. I put this pick out on my Twitter at 20/1, and it has already been backed in to 12's.

Commendation is a 3 year-old filly trained by Michael Keady. She is 1 from 2 for her new yard. Her win came from the same course and was an impressive 4 length win, the other outing was against a very strong field. She has a good draw and favourable weight with a 7lb claiming jockey on top. Good each way chance.

If you're prepared to forgive SPIRITUALISM's last run out, a first in 129 days, then she might be able to strip fitter returning to the polytrack surface she won on at Kempton at the end of last year. That was from only two pounds lighter in the weights. Her only win was recorded wearing blinkers, which return today, and I like the booking of Luke Morris too. Could fare better racing against her own sex.
Good second a few starts back. Not done well since then, but this CD could see her in a better light. Conditions to suit.

Prince Rasam lines up off 70 for Michael Bell, who holds a solid 18% strike rate in all-weather handicaps at Lingfield over the past ten years showing a level stakes profit of 4% at SP. Drawn in stall 1 with Kieran Shoemark booked, he’s well positioned to make a bold bid in a winnable Class 5.
Largely consistent for grade achieiving appropiate average times for the grade second last time out to inform horse appreciating the Course and Distance recent rpr improviong .
Very good record in these events, but first run of this season minus headgear. Has won over course and distance previously, and if fresh race ready, can place.

C&D Victor in January. Last seen finishing 7th of 9 in a Wolverhampton handicap 28 days ago. Now, equipped with cheekpieces, she might show improvement if the new gear has the right impact. An each-way wager at 16/1 is recommended.

Fat Gladiator teams up with jockey P Cosgrave who has a good record in handicaps when riding for this yard (117 runs, 13 wins, 11% strike rate, +27pts @ 23% ROI). Stepping up to a mile today could suit his running style, and with Cosgrave’s expertise, they might make a notable impact.
Poor strike rate, but goes well over course and distance and has run well fresh. £1 lb claim helps and didn't run badly over 10f here when last seen.

Love Your Work looks to have solid claims based on recent form and the yard's good record in all weather handicaps at this time of year (D Holland, AW handicaps, Spring: 79 runs, 14 wins, 18% strike rate, +25pts @ 31% ROI). He’s a consistent sort on the all-weather and comes into this off a decent effort over course and distance. He’s well drawn and has winning form at this level, so if he gets a decent pace to aim at, he should be right there at the finish.
Finished 5th in a decent race a few starts back. Not done much since, but an unexposed horse who could go much better here.
outpaced over 7f lastime in what looked a strong race for this grade as 1st 2nd and 3rd in good form and 1st has run well next time out . Has CD form and apprentice on taking 7lb off .

Lost his way a bit this winter, but BLUE COLLAR LAD's mark now drops to below the last winning mark on Chelmsford's polytrack last September. That poor run was uncharacteristic and maybe he's one to keep an eye on in case of a revival. Won or placed on six of ten runs here, so returns to a favourable track.

Galel looks poised for a big run here with this race representing a drop in class to a very thin looking class 6 handicap and a step back up in trip both those factors being good moves by his connections currently operating on a mark of 55 this daughter of Exceed And Excel & Gallipot ( Dam's sire Galileo ) is likely to be much better than a mark of 55 and is likely to have a big performance in the locker just waiting to be unleashed in very good time jockey David Egan takes the ride that being another positive and he can greatly assist Galel in showcasing a much better piece of form this time out needs considering in a race of this nature

Was a little disappointing when 3rd at Newcastle last time when holding a good position into the final furlong but never quickened away. A 6-time winner who is very consistent, and it's interesting that an extra 3lb pull with jockey Jack Doughty taking over the ride.

Alice Haynes has a fair record with her all-weather handicap runners at Lingfield: 17 wins from 122 runs for a 14% strike rate and +20pts @ 16% ROI. The A/E of 0.86 suggest her runners are generally performing close to expectations. Mashaan fits that mold as he’s consistent and capable in this grade, and with the yard’s decent record at the track, he’s definitely worth a look.

Back on last winning mark after running a really good race last time out, especially as badly hampered in the final furlong, preventing a closer finish. A repeat of that run with better luck and a smoother patch should put him there at the finish.

With 4 victories at this course, including a win in January, this 7-year-old has promise. However, his last 3 performances have been sub-par, culminating in a last place finish in a Wolverhampton handicap just 12 days ago. A return to this venue is crucial for his comeback. Consider placing an each-way bet at 12/1.
Course and distance winner. Should lead from the front, getting two pounds from the favorite, so must be taken seriously. Good jockey on board. Nap Win.
Stable in decent nick, 7 from 26 in March, and selection was still very green when demolishing his field in December, with the promise of plenty more to come.
Cosmic View has winning form at this distance and class, thrives on similar going and performs well in current headgear. He also holds solid claims.
Shaped much better than the bare result last time, having met trouble in running from the home straight and had no chance. Finished full of running and comes here off the same mark.
Brinton won a few starts ago at Southwell over 1m. The form looks okay, and he has been consistent of late. Probably doesn't need to improve much to figure. Well drawn.

Venus Slipper demonstrated her proficiency over this specific course and distance by securing a victory at Lingfield over 1 mile and 2 furlongs on the Polytrack just last month, on February 16th. This proven track and distance form is a critical advantage, indicating her suitability and ability to perform well under these exact race conditions.

Danehill Star shaped with some promise last time out and returns to handicap company now where he’s open to improvement, especially over this trip. If he settles well and handles the surface, he could take a step forward at a decent price.
Meets a few horses that have placed recently and gone well. This one is more of a back class type who is starting to become well handicapped. CD will suit.

Limmortale looks to be turning a corner coming off a solid second at Wolverhampton just a week ago and had run a close third at Dundalk before that, showing clear signs of improvement since switching yards. In a modest classified stakes like this, his recent form stands out, and if he holds that level, he’s got a big chance of going one better.

Firstly, his proven track record at Lingfield over the one-mile-two-furlong distance is a significant advantage. His victory in September 2024 and his recent second-place finish in February 2025 over the same course and distance demonstrate a clear affinity for the Lingfield Polytrack and this specific trip.

The 4-year-old showed a moderate performance, finishing 7th out of 11 in a handicap race at Southwell over a mile last December. Now, stepping up in distance, it will require a big effort, but with John Egan, who has secured 14 wins and 46 places here, in the saddle, an each-way bet at 14/1 could yield a good run.

Briefly gets weight from her two rivals here despite the handicapper deciding to put her up six pounds after finishing a half-length 2nd of 9 to Badbury Rings over course and distance last month, running after a six-month break. It is her two rivals who arrive from a break this time.

She tends to run well following a break of 3+ months with a record of 1st, 5th, 2nd in her 3 times that has happened. The 5th came in Listed company of 15, so it was still respectable. The run last time out was more likely due to the quick reappearance rather than the 3m trip. Following a break and faster ground should see her in better light.

Mr Mackay has not run over this far before but likes the better going. He won over two miles three and a half furlongs on good at Huntingdon back in 2023. In this four-horse race, the pace is not likely to be strong, and Toby McCain-Mitchell is a good jockey for his three-pound claim.

He has won 3 races over hurdles over a multitude of trips including over 2m5f at Fontwell on his penultimate start. His 3rd last time out was still encouraging and he should continue his upward trajectory especially against some rivals not proven over this distance.

Recently changed trainer to Paul Nicholls. Placed second in a race in France after a longer distance. Making its first appearance with a Hood, hopefully, should make a difference and get him off to a strong career.

Point winner Disguisedlimit has proven to be a weak finisher in all three of his hurdle races after running prominently. He was beaten into third place at Taunton by an ex-French Paul Nicholls horse, Fasol, last time and has Paul Nicholls' Zaochen Enki to beat this time. But he has yet to run in the UK, and his only run was 233 days ago in France when 2nd in a hurdle. He could need the run at Wincanton, and Disguisedlimit may find it easier to hold onto the lead on a fast surface.

Barford Groover was a close second in a bumper back in 2023 but then had a whopping 642-day break. He returned in January, understandably at the back of the pack, and could improve now, second up and running for another new yard with Sean back on top, who was in charge for that run to second. EW 2P.

The 6-year-old showed promise with a runner-up finish in a bumper at Plumpton last winter, but has not been able to maintain that momentum, especially during three mares' novice hurdles in November and December. Now, following a move from the O'Neill stable, it is set to make her first appearance in three months. Betting each-way at 33/1 could offer value.
Has had four runs and needs to put his best foot forward today to have any chance of winning this. Looks well-bred and CD should suit.
3 runs and not done a lot, but can still improve. Is well-bred, and the trainer and jockey get on well together.

Space Voyage has to carry a seven-pound penalty for her easy win at Market Rasen last week. She was held up until the final bend but took it up three out and then eased away from the field. She could be rated even higher. Beau M Morgan takes off his five-pound allowance to take her weight down to twelve stone four pounds, but she still has to give weight to the field.

Still winless over fences, a streak dating back 18 months, but he has been better of late. His last 2 races were 2nd to 2 next time out winners, so he is more than capable of winning from this mark and has won on good ground over hurdles previously.

She won twice over 3m1f on good ground last year, followed that up with a 2nd and 3rd and then disappointed when pulling up at Fakenham with the step up to class 2 looking a step too far. She drops down to a Class 4 today and reappears on the same mark as her 2nd in Leicester and should run well.

Made a few costly jumping errors at crucial times on chase debut at Southwell in early December, and although finishing 3rd, it was an encouraging start. Has shown better form over hurdles on better ground, so I'm looking for a better run today in a race that he can dominate from the front.

Tipping Somespring Special here. Not in the best of form last season, but backing that another change of trainer and an 8-month layoff will bring her back sharp for this one. Worth noting that the favorite tends to jump to the left, and this is a right-handed track.

She finished a solid 4th on her handicap hurdle debut and has since switched to the flat, with a 1st and 2nd at Wolverhampton in that time over 2m. She reverts to hurdles today and now takes advantage of a 2lbs lower mark than her hurdles debut and has a chance.

Queen All Star enters this race with a promising profile, having secured a win and a good third-place finish in her two starts as a two-year-old. While returning from a layoff, the comment that she 'sets the standard' suggests she is considered a high-quality runner by her stable.

Vamp lines up in the 5:30 at Wolverhampton and looks a live contender. She’s placed in her last two starts over similar trips, and now returns to the same course and distance where she ran a close second when last seen. She’s drawn nicely, and this looks no stronger than what she’s been contesting. With conditions to suit and confidence behind her, she’s got a solid chance of breaking through.
Ran too fast over seven furlongs first time out two weeks ago. Providing he settles better in this lower class contest over two furlongs shorter, he should see a significant improvement.
Not as well-bred as a few in here, but still, there have been a fair few shocks over the last few days, and this one could be another. Well drawn and could like the CD.
Green Team showed improved form over twelve furlongs, finishing strongly last time out at this course. It should go close to following up as the extra furlong should not be a problem.

Wannabe Brave has a decent shout if bouncing back to his best. He’s a course winner and stays this 2-mile trip well, which is a big plus in this kind of race. His recent runs have been a bit below par, but he’s now 2lb below his last winning mark, and a return to a track he likes could spark a better run.

Fashionelle is a 6-year-old mare trained by Tony Forbes. She was a jumps horse with Fergal O'Brien, now turned flat horse. She won her debut outing in a novice race at Wolverhampton over 1m 1/2f but later found trouble when upping in class over the same distance, finishing 8th from 12. When upped to today's trip, she has shown nice improvement in just 2 runs. First, finishing 5th from 9 on 1st March and 10 days later finishing 3rd from 10 runners. She has a good chance here running off 58 with a 3lb claiming jockey onboard. She is also drawn 1, so has a good chance to position herself accordingly.

The Rebecca Menzie trained Show No Fear won over 2m 56y at Newcastle, then finished last of 6 in handicap over the same c&d 12 days ago. He led, ridden and pressed for lead 2f out, soon headed and dropped to 3rd, weakened inside final furlong. The drop back in trip this evening to 1m 5f 219y looks ideal and I think there is still room to improve off his current mark of 67 in this grade. Young winning jockey Kaiya Fraser keeps the ride and can take off a valuable 3lbs.

She won on her last start, which came at this track. However, that was over 1m1f, and she steps up to 1m4f. Her pedigree suggests she should comfortably win, as she is a half-sister to seven winners, including 1m2f-2m4f Big Orange, 1m4f AW Lydford, and 1m4f winner India. So this trip should be ideal.

Tuscan Star looks like an improving type. She’s lightly raced and shaped nicely when third on handicap debut over this course and distance last time out. That run suggested there’s more to come, and with a clearer run this time, she could easily step forward. Still unexposed and open to progress, she looks a solid bet in a field where plenty have questions to answer.
A strong horse with a lot of experience under its saddle. Shouldn't have too many issues with the extra weight on board. Has recently dropped in official rating but shouldn't matter too much.

Winner over 8.5f here in January. Mostly solid efforts in defeat since, including when not beaten far in 3rd at Southwell last time. I can't see any reason why he shouldn't be bang there once again this evening.

Bobby Joe Leg lines up in the 7:00 at Wolverhampton and you always have to respect this veteran in low-grade handicaps. He’s a regular on the all-weather and has racked up plenty of wins over the years, including at this track. He’s back down to a workable mark and wasn’t beaten far here last time, so he’s clearly still got some fire in him. If he gets a decent early position, he’s more than capable of landing a blow in a race like this.

Selection reunited with Muscutt, who won on him in 2023. Comes here off a falling mark after running over an inadequate test the last twice. Last won 7 months ago on turf from a mark of 76. Comes here off 70, back up in trip, and has run well enough around here in the past.

Has decent form around here. Unlucky not to follow up and complete a hat trick of wins here in January, when meeting trouble in running and finishing 3rd. Comes here off the same mark and has a decent each-way chance.

Thapa VC gets a kindly drop in grade and hasn't been running that bad under Jack Mitchell. But it gets a good jockey change here in Rossa Ryan, which can only help its cause as it continues to fall in weight. Good each way.

Course and distance winner who was last seen at Southwell 20 days ago where finishing 9th/12 however this gelded son of Zoustar is no horse to overlook and he is the type to bounce back quickly especially having found a suitable looking race to get involved in here currently operating on a mark of 66 which is well within his capabilities expect to see Zu Run thundering home in the closing argument of this class 5 handicap with jockey Billy Loughnane taking ride that most certainly being a positive merits consideration

Harbour Vision might be getting on a bit but did win two last November off a 58 and a 61. He was a decent second in February on a 66. Although a bit duff last time out, that was in C4. I think the return to C5 off a 66 with Mikkel in the saddle, claiming 5 lbs, could be worth an EW chance.

Ziggys Condor looks like one on the up. He made a winning handicap debut over course and distance last time, staying on strongly and shaping like there’s more to come. He’s been nudged up in the weights but did it well enough to suggest he can handle the rise. Still lightly raced and clearly suited to this surface, he’s a major threat if showing the same spark again.

Supreme King has solid claims if repeating his recent efforts. He’s been in consistent form this winter, knocking on the door a few times and going close at this level. He handles the surface well and stays the trip, plus he’s got a nice draw to work from. With conditions in his favour and the form to back it up, he looks like a serious player in this one.

I like the look of Twilight Romance at this price. He has been competing in better races than this, and his last race, also at Wolverhampton, looked like a strong race to me. This is his third outing after a long break and wind surgery, and I think he will be ready to roll.

Very strong each-way bet here. Makes seasonal reappearance after 5 months off and would have gone close to winning at the beginning of last season, after a similar break, going very well when denied a run. Looked unlucky. That was a Class 2 race off 83. This race today is a Class 4 and he runs off 79. Tapeta debut, should be okay on it as he handles polytrack.

Billy Loughnane usually gets a big-priced one in, so why not try one not seen for a while or had just the one AW run... Jungle Land! Now, the stable took this race last year. Will lightning strike twice?

Gunfighter is the rank outsider here but is 2 from 3 on Tapeta and is only 3lb higher than his last win, which was an easy one on his last visit to this course. He makes his 4-year-old debut here, and the first-time booking of David Probert is a good one for the horse's new stable since he rides this course well. Gunfighter also should have the early pace to make the most of being drawn in stall 4, and 14/1 looks decent value.

His last triumph occurred at Chelmsford in February. A month ago, he placed 4th among 7 competitors in a handicap race at Chelmsford, covering 5 furlongs. As he moves up in distance, he must elevate his performance. Nevertheless, with the trainer performing well and the jockey providing a 5lb advantage, the 16/1 odds each-way for the distance winner appear to be a solid wager.

Raft Up looks like a live contender in a weak race. He’s been holding his form reasonably well in similar low grade contests and has a decent bit of course experience. While he’s yet to get his head in front, he’s been running on well late and the step back up to 7f could suit.
Heartrate had a nice win by a neck last time out over course and distance. Gone up to a mark of 52, can win again!
Raul de Silva gave Shamardia an excellent run LTO when finishing second behind Stella Hogan, who went on to place third in a tough Class 5 race. I think we will see him being in the mix again.

Red Walls last won in January, running off a 46 with Ed in the saddle and gets back to the same mark today with him back on top. Worth a chance as did win here early last year off a 49 so we know he can handle the Poly EW.
C&D winner on her only other start from a pound higher last July. She made all of the running that day and has been drawn in one here so is perfectly drawn to attack early again.

Caelan runs in the 8:30 at Wolverhampton and looks a big player if building on recent form. He’s been running consistently well and was a close second last time over this same course and distance. That run showed he handles the track and trip perfectly, and he’s edging closer to getting his head back in front.
